newsitem.title: GERMANY: German court bans extremist protest in Luebeck.
newsitem.headline: German court bans extremist protest in Luebeck.

text.p: A German court on Friday upheld a ban on two rallies by right-wing extremists in the northern city of Luebeck, where neo-Nazis are suspected of carrying out a recent arson attack on a church.
The court cited the "particular climate" in the city following last weekend's attack as its reason for banning the rallies scheduled for Saturday morning.

An anti-racist alliance has also said it plans to demonsrate in Luebeck on Saturday. Police have said they fear clashes between the groups and have promised hundreds of officers will be on duty in case of trouble.
The right-wingers appealed to the court after city authorities had banned their rallies earlier this week. But the court said the city's action was correct.
The arson attackers daubed swastikas on the facade of the St Vicelin church and also scrawled the name of a local priest whose parish is sheltering a family of Algerian asylum-seekers.
